items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 10:30AM AKST until November 28 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels 1.5 to 3.0 feet above
the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk and Kwigillingok

* WHEN...6 PM Thursday to 6 AM Saturday. Particularly the
overnight tide cycles Thursday night and Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including
lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of southerly winds combined
with the high tide cycle will increase the potential for

items.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 25 at 7:52AM AKST until November 27 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...No additional falling snow is expected. Strong
winds will blow snow already on the ground to create areas of low
visibility near the surface. A brief decrease in winds is expected
Wednesday before winds strengthen once more Thursday.
items.instruction:
Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 24 at 1:23PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The Department of Environmental Conservation has issued an Air
Quality Alert which is IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM AKST THURSDAY.

North Pole has a Stage 2 alert.

Fairbanks has no alert.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 1:10PM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Tidal levels across the panhandle are expected to be running high
for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Wind direction,
magnitude, and timing with these systems will be monitored closely as
a combination of high tide and winds in an onshore direction
could lead to tides exceeding astronomical high tide by a foot or
more.
